card.title: P D S F  ·  build your software factory

lines.simulated: You type the real commands. The agent is SIMULATED.

card.footer: Ctrl-C quits at any time · re-run the command to resume where you stopped

coach: Build an agentic software factory on a real project.
About 10 min · no token spent · nothing installed outside its workspace.

steps.name: the install command
coach: This is Blackbelt, a small Node app. First, install PDSF in it.
Same command you will run on your own project tomorrow.
steps.cta: Type the command (Tab ⇥ fills it in)
steps.hint: Press Tab: it types the install command for you. Then Enter.
done: Installed. {skills} skills, one commit. Nothing outside this folder.

coach: Open this folder in your IDE, with the file tree and the git graph:
files and commits will appear there as you go.
steps.cta: Type code .  ·  s skips it (no IDE here)
steps.hint: code . opens VS Code. Another IDE? Open the folder in it, then type s.
done: {ide} is open on {ws}. Keep an eye on it.
skipped: No IDE for now: open {ws} in any editor later.

coach: Now start the agent. Here, claude is a stand-in: it replays recorded
real sessions. 0 token, and your real claude is untouched.
steps.hint: Type claude, then Enter: the screen switches to the simulated harness.
done: You are in the harness. Same look as Claude Code, but simulated.

coach: Ask the harness what it can do: each PDSF skill is a slash command.
done: /build-factory comes first: it sets the factory up on this repo.

help.build-factory: wire the backlogs, bootstrap the context
help.grill-with-docs: design a user story with you

coach: Build the factory. The agent will ask you 2 questions about this repo.
Pick with ↑ ↓ and Enter. The recorded run's answer is preselected.
steps.hint: Type /build-factory (Tab fills it in), then Enter.

play.tool: Bash(git remote -v; ls -la; ls docs docs/agents …)

play.say: Existing project, no remote. I'll start in Scaffold mode.

play.ask: A — Business backlog. Where do your user stories live?
choices: business-backlog/ — markdown files (found in the repo)

play.ask: B — Technical backlog. Where should agents write their tickets?

play.say: Triage labels: the defaults. Domain docs: single context.

done: Scaffold done: 2 backlogs wired, {files} files, 1 commit. Look in your IDE.

coach: Next step in a fresh session: a short context means a focused agent.
Less context, fewer hallucinations. /clear, then /build-factory again.
Start a fresh session: clear the agent's context.
steps.hint: Type /clear, then Enter. It empties the session, not your files.
done: Context cleared. The agent forgot this session; files and commits stay.
Now run /build-factory again: it sees the scaffold is done, moves on.

coach: Same command, fresh session: now it builds the domain context.
The agent will ask you 1 question.
steps.hint: Type /build-factory again (Tab fills it in), then Enter.

play.tool: Bash(cat README.md package.json; for f in src/*.js; do …)

play.say: Scaffold is done → Context mode. First, the core language:

play.ask: The code says "belt" for the rank and for the attempt. What is a Belt?
choices: The attempt; the rank is its Colour (recommended)

play.say: (The recorded run went on: 9 more answers, as recommended.)

writes.note: glossary: Belt, Colour, Submission, Mentor, Sensei …

done: Context written: a glossary and {adrs} ADRs. Agents now speak your domain.

coach: Last one: check the factory's health.

play.tool: Bash(ls -la; ls docs docs/agents docs/adr; git check-ignore …)

play.na: 2 n/a (local backlog: no labels, no logins)

done: 🎉 Your factory is built. 8 checks green, {commits} commits.

lines.dim: (the full install command is printed when you quit)

coach: That's it. Tomorrow, on your project: install, then /build-factory.
